title: Point 4D Transformer Networks for Spatio-Temporal Modeling in Point Cloud Videos
research_problem: Modeling the spatio-temporal structure in raw point cloud videos is challenging due to their irregular, unordered, and inconsistent nature across frames. Existing solutions like voxelization are computationally inefficient, and point tracking is difficult and may fail without point colors.
core_idea: To avoid point tracking, we propose a Point 4D Transformer (P4Transformer) network that uses a point 4D convolution to embed spatio-temporal local structures and a transformer to capture global appearance and motion information via self-attention on the embedded local features.

method_modules.name: Point 4D Convolution
method_modules.description: Encodes spatio-temporal local structures in a point cloud video and subsamples points. It is performed directly on raw points without voxelization. It uses a parameterized function to generate kernels for all potential displacements based on spatial radius (rs) and temporal radius (rt).

evidence.quote_or_summary: We propose a point 4D convolution to extract local structure and subsample points to be processed by the subsequent transformer... Our point 4D convolution is directly performed on raw points without voxelization... The function ζ is a parameterized function of (δx, δy, δz, δt) to generate kernels based on input displacements.

method_modules.name: Transformer
method_modules.description: Captures global appearance and motion information across the entire video by performing video-level self-attention on the embedded local features from the point 4D convolution. It merges related local areas based on attention weights rather than explicit tracking.

evidence.quote_or_summary: We employ a transformer to capture the spatio-temporal structure of raw point cloud videos... We perform self-attention on I... The softmax function is performed on the entire video, which is referred to as video-level self-attention.

method_modules.name: Application Heads
method_modules.description: The network is applied to two tasks: 3D action recognition (video-level classification) and 4D semantic segmentation (point-level prediction). For action recognition, a max pooling and MLP are used. For segmentation, feature propagation layers recover subsampled points to original points.

evidence.quote_or_summary: We show how to apply our P4Transformer to 3D action recognition and 4D semantic segmentation... For action recognition: A max pooling merges local features to a global feature, which is then mapped to action predictions by an MLP. For segmentation: feature propagation layers recover the subsampled N′ points to the original N points by interpolating features.

reproduction_risks: The paper assumes point features (Ft) are available for the generic network, but notes that for some datasets (MSR-Action3D, NTU RGB+D 60, NTU RGB+D 120) Ft is not provided. The implementation for when Ft is not available is simpler (ζ = Wd · (δx, δy, δz, δt)T), which may affect performance.

The point 4D convolution construction involves several hyperparameters (temporal radius rt, temporal stride st, spatial radius rs, spatial subsampling rate ss) that are not specified in the provided text.
The transformer's self-attention is computed over the entire video (L′N′ elements), which could be memory-intensive for long videos with many points.
Exact training details (optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs) are not provided in the given text.
